decision_text: Prompt v5 stays unchanged. The v6 digits candidate regressed fidelity on one private take and over-converted an idiom in one synthetic repeat.
request: Operator chose digits for spoken numbers; conductor asked for one added rule, kept only if no fidelity case regressed and non-number strict count did not drop.

protocol.provider_guards: Fallbacks disabled and provider.max_price enforced; the application sends neither.
protocol.rule: - Write spoken numbers, dates, times, and quantities as digits: `three hundred and twenty five servers, March fourth` becomes `325 servers, March 4`. Keep numbers that are part of a name, idiom, or quotation as spoken.
protocol.v6_edits: Added the digits rule and removed "and their written form" from the numbers-preservation sentence.

corpus.precommit: Digit-form accepted strings and four new public cases were written before any v6 call. Ordinal, one-paragraph and list-count cases accepted both forms; the first/second-sentence case stayed non-number and unchanged.

protocol.private_comparison: 16 fresh v6 outputs against the retained frozen v5 outputs, graded by the builder with spoken-number conversions visible. This is not a fully blind comparison.

keep_rule.fidelity: No v6 private or synthetic output may have a hard fidelity failure that v5 did not have on the same case; number over-conversion in a name, idiom or quotation and wrong numeric value are hard failures.
keep_rule.strict: v6 strict exact-accepted count on non-number cases must be >= the same-session v5 control count; also report against the earlier frozen v5 run.
keep_rule.number_cases: Digit compliance on the number cases is reported separately and cannot rescue a fidelity regression.
keep_rule.otherwise: Ship v5 unchanged and record the failure on the decision record.

protocol.independence: The public core cases were reused from earlier tuning; one builder agent graded. One draw per private take, so sampling noise and rule effect are not separated.

public_fidelity.non_hard_digit_misses: minimum-and-option wrote the ordinal as 4th in two repeats; accepted strings required "a fourth".

private_fidelity.note: One v6 output had class distinct_claim_omitted. One other v6 output had class minor_attribution_shift, which the builder did not count as a hard failure. No private spoken number was converted to a wrong value; clear cardinal quantities became digits.
private_fidelity.limits: The same class of failure appeared once in the earlier v4 prompt, so [INFERRED] it may be sampling noise rather than a digit-rule effect. This trial cannot establish that.

results.rule_effect: [MEASURED] Clear cardinal quantities, dates and version strings became digits in every v6 repeat except one idiom repeat and the ordinal case; [INFERRED] the rule is promising but needs idiom protection and repeated private takes before adoption.

accounting.attribution: The trial delta equals the reported cost of its calls; earlier shared-key QA usage remains in the cumulative total.

limitations: [MEASURED] One operator, one grader, three public repeats, one private draw per take.
[UNVERIFIED] No live app, delivery, build or local test path was exercised.
[MEASURED] Public and aggregate evidence only: no private text, take identifier or vocabulary list is in this receipt.
